subject: MSA & Order Form: proposal for output rights and training-use
messages:
From: Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: MSA + Order Form — follow-up on IP and training use

Rachel,

Thanks for the demo last week — the product looks promising. Our legal team has a couple of open items in the Order Form/MSA around output ownership and any license to use customer content for training. I've attached our redlines to the Order Form (see Acme_OrderForm_Counter_2027-03-01.pdf).

Two specific asks from Acme legal:
- Confirm whether Acme retains all Output rights (generated text/files) and whether Redwood will ever claim ownership.
- Clarify the scope of any training/feedback license — Acme is uncomfortable with a broad license to use customer prompts/outputs to train models for commercial use.

Can you share Redwood's standard wording and whether you can accept a carve-out that prevents Outputs from being used to train public/commercial models? Also, please flag any items that would require exec/legal escalation.

Best,
Susan Lee
Head of Procurement, Acme Corp
[attachment: Acme_OrderForm_Counter_2027-03-01.pdf]

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Susan Lee <susan.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 15:30:00 -0500
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form — follow-up on IP and training use

Thanks, Susan — appreciate the clear redlines. We've reviewed and I wanted to summarize Redwood's commercial position so your legal team has a concise starting point. Attached is a marked-up MSA with our proposed language (Redwood_MSA_Redlines_v1.docx).

High-level positions:
- Outputs: Customer retains all right, title and interest in Outputs produced from Customer Content. Redwood will not claim ownership of Customer Outputs.
- Training / Feedback License: Redwood requests a limited, revocable feedback license to use de-identified usage data and explicit customer-submitted feedback to improve service quality, safety, and non-customer-facing model behavior. This is not a broad license to incorporate Customer Content or Outputs into public/commercial model training unless expressly agreed in writing.
- Opt-out / Data Handling: We can add an opt-out mechanism for training use on an account basis and agree to specified retention periods and deletion upon request for PII.

If Acme needs a stricter prohibition (e.g., no use of Outputs for any model training), we can escalate but will need to check impact to our safety tooling and analytics. Happy to jump on a 30-minute call with your counsel + ours to walk through carve-outs. Proposed times: Tue 3/2 10am ET or Wed 3/3 2pm ET.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Confirm whether Acme's redline intends to prohibit all training/use of Outputs or to limit commercial model training only.
2) If prohibition is required, I will loop in Markus from Legal to propose compromise language.
3) If acceptable, we produce final redline and push to DocuSign.

-Rachel
Rachel Kim
Enterprise Accounts, Redwood Inference
[attachment: Redwood_MSA_Redlines_v1.docx]

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 10:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form — legal suggestion on IP / feedback license

Rachel / Marissa — I reviewed Acme's counter and Rachel's proposed compromise. Below are recommended edits and rationale you can present. I've also attached a short guidance memo (Redwood_Legal_IP_guide_v1.pdf) for negotiation points.

Recommended customer-facing clause (sample):
"Customer retains all rights in Customer Content and Outputs. Redwood may use de-identified, aggregated telemetry and Customer-submitted feedback to improve the Service, including safety testing and internal model tuning, provided that Redwood shall not use Customer Content or Outputs to train or create models that are sold or otherwise commercially distributed outside Redwood's internal product safety improvements without Customer's prior written consent."

Key negotiation levers:
- "De-identified and aggregated" limits risk that PII or proprietary prompts are used directly.
- Narrow the purpose to "service improvements and safety" rather than product training for commercial models.
- Offer an account-level opt-out for training use in exchange for a modest price adjustment or SLA credit.
- Audit rights: Acme is likely to ask for audit or attestation; we can offer an annual security attestation and a limited on-site/virtual audit for high-tier customers.

If Acme insists on an absolute ban on any use of Outputs for model development, that materially impacts our ability to improve models and may require a bespoke pricing and operational guardrails (e.g., dedicated capacity, separate logging). We should signal that as a potential commercial trade.

Happy to join the call.
-Markus
General Counsel, Redwood Inference
[attachment: Redwood_Legal_IP_guide_v1.pdf]

From: Susan Lee <susan.lee@acme.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acme.com>, legal@acme.com
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 13:42:00 -0500
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form — follow-up on IP and training use

Rachel / Markus — thanks for the quick turn. Acme's position summarized: we will not agree to any clause that allows Outputs or Customer Content to be used to train models that may be commercially released without explicit customer consent. We can accept a limited use for internal service improvement provided that:
1) Redwood explicitly commits that Customer Content and Outputs will never be used to train public/commercial models;
2) Redwood provides an opt-out toggle at the account level that prevents any use of the account's data for model tuning;
3) Redwood agrees to a 12-month data retention maximum for raw prompts (unless otherwise required for ongoing investigations) and deletion upon request; and
4) Redwood provides an annual attestation covering the above, and a limited verification right for Acme (virtual inspection).

If Redwood confirms these items in writing, Acme will sign the Order Form. We also request a modest SLA credit for the additional contractual restriction.

Attached is a one-page summary of our changes; happy to discuss on the call.

-Susan
Head of Procurement, Acme Corp
[attachment: Acme_OrderForm_Counter_2027-03-02.pdf]

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Susan Lee <susan.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 16:10:00 -0500
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form — follow-up on IP and training use

Susan — this is helpful and close to what we expected. Thanks for laying out the four items clearly. Proposed path forward:

1) Redwood Legal will prepare a focused redline reflecting the sample language Markus proposed and will incorporate the opt-out and retention commitments you listed. We will also propose an annual attestation rather than an on-demand audit (we can scope a limited virtual verification for enterprise customers if needed).

2) Regarding the SLA credit: we can offer a one-time account credit in lieu of taking on an ongoing penalty structure; Markus will include suggested language in the redline.

3) Call to finalize: Tue 3/3 10am ET works for our team. Please confirm and send calendar invite with counsel included.

I'll have the redline back to you by end of day tomorrow so you have time to review prior to the call. If Acme wants an absolute prohibition on any use of Outputs for model development (without exceptions), Markus notes that will likely require a dedicated deployment or pricing adjustment — we can surface cost implications if that comes up.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out.

-Rachel Kim
Enterprise Accounts, Redwood Inference
[signature block]
body_summary: Procurement from Acme raised output ownership and training license concerns. Redwood (Rachel) proposed customer-retains-output + limited de-identified feedback license with opt-out. Legal (Markus) suggested compromise language limiting use to safety/service improvements and opt-out with potential commercial trade. Acme responded with conditions (explicit ban on training for commercial models, opt-out, retention max, attestation). Rachel proposed redline and call to finalize; next steps include Redwood legal redline and DocuSign prep.
